newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU foreign ministers wait and see on French stand.
newsitem.headline: EU foreign ministers wait and see on French stand.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers reacted cautiously on Monday to news of the French Socialists' sweeping victory in Sunday's elections and its possible impact on economic and monetary union (EMU).

Arriving for a routine meeting to discuss the draft treaty to be agreed at the EU's Amsterdam summit in two weeks, ministers played down any possible negative impact of the left's triumph on the treaty review or to the timetable for EMU.
"I don't know, it depends who will be foreign minister," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo told reporters on arrival. The Netherlands currently holds the rotating EU presidency.
Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Helm-Wallens, welcoming the election of a Socialist government in France, said it was important to stick to the timetable for EMU.
Asked about whether the Socialist victory could force a delay, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said it was too early to say.

"This is much too early for me to predict...We have to wait and see what position the new French government will take in this respect," he told reporters, adding that "mixed signals" had been given during the election campaign.

Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel predicted no significant change in the outcome of the EU treaty review, as the concerns expressed by the French Socialists for a more social EU role were being met in a new chapter on employment.
"I don't see any changes," he said.
